summary: Before claiming that a change to how you remember, find or decide made things better: how to measure it, and what the figures do and do not let you say.
triggers: measure whether a change of memory or recall helps
exam score before and after a mutation of the memory
does this improve recall finding retrieval ranking
benchmark evaluate compare my change on the journal
the gate says the candidate remembers worse
what does this figure percentage metric show
exclusions: A change with no claim about quality: a rename, a comment, a move of code that the tests already hold.
A fault with one right answer that a test can state: write the test.
assumptions: The journal can be copied and the copy asked without touching the running store.
The exam's questions are in the journal, and one in four of them is held out of the index (heldOut in brain/recall.ts).
A figure is only as good as what was compared: the same copy and the same questions before and after.
